title: AUTH: Expire stalled Supabase session-cache promises
head: fix/auth-session-cache-expiry-20261109
body: The shared `getCachedSession()` memoizes a pending Supabase `getSession()` promise and only clears it on resolution, rejection, or an auth event. If a Safari refresh/read hangs without an event, the dashboard's 12-second timeout shows recovery UI but Retry reuses the same unresolved promise. Expire cached reads after 12 seconds so subsequent retry can issue a fresh read; keep auth event invalidation and existing authorization behavior. This does not claim to solve underlying Supabase lock stalls. Await CI and launch gate.

title: [DRAFT] Safety, account deletion, verification, public career pages and language
head: feat/safety-deletion-verification-public-career-language
body:
## Status: NOT READY TO MERGE

This draft tracks the in-progress SAFE-1 / DEL-1 / VER-1 / PROPASS-1 / LANG-1 work.

### Latest safety change
- Replaced the legacy destructive `POST /api/account/delete` handler on this branch with a fail-closed 409 response. It no longer cancels Stripe, removes storage, or deletes Auth users. This is a temporary safeguard only; it is not the completed 30-day deletion lifecycle.

### Current branch contents
- Language-provider improvements: locale registry validation, browser-language fallback for signed-out users, account preference precedence and readable fallback.
- DEL-1 implementation notes, 30-day deletion-request ledger migration (not applied to Supabase), and live production foreign-key audit.
- Cross-workstream implementation gap audit.

### Blocking acceptance criteria
- [ ] DEL-1: password re-verification, 30-day request/cancel lifecycle, sign-in cancellation, write restrictions, safe finalizer, review anonymization, retention of subscriptions/moderation history, tests.
- [ ] SAFE-1: unified reporting across all requested content, blocking and mutual interaction enforcement, consistent moderation hold pipeline, admin queue/actions/audit/notifications.
- [ ] VER-1: player-only single-proof flow, private evidence access review, approve/reject reasons, notifications, resubmission and suspension behavior.
- [ ] PROPASS-1: default-off public career page, strict public-field allowlist, disabled-page 404 and share card.
- [ ] LANG-1: complete key coverage and locale formatting/runtime tests on all target UI surfaces.
- [ ] Run lint, typecheck, build, migrations/RLS tests, API tests and end-to-end tests.

Do not merge or deploy this branch as a completed release until every blocking item is implemented and verified. The deletion migration remains unapplied and no production data has been modified.

title: Fix desktop header collisions and establish shared desktop layout
head: fix/desktop-layout-system
body:
## Summary
- Replace the overlapping absolute-positioned desktop header layout with a shared three-group flex header at 64px.
- Keep the desktop header hidden below 1024px; leave the mobile bottom navigation component untouched.
- Add a shared desktop content frame, spacing/grid rules, and theme-token-aware dropdown surface.
- Add a Playwright DOM overlap/screenshot audit script (`npm run audit:desktop-overlap`) that requires real route paths via `ROUTES_JSON`.

## Root-cause diagnosis
The previous `app/hoopcheck-preview-system.css` rules positioned `.hc-header-nav` absolutely with `inset: 0` and `width: 100%`, while `.hc-header-actions` was separately absolutely positioned at the right edge. The nav therefore occupied the same horizontal rectangle as both the logo and action controls; `pointer-events` did not reserve layout space. The brand was raised with `z-index: 2`, masking rather than correcting the collision. The header also inherited multiple competing responsive header rules from older CSS layers.

## Verification limits
The overlap audit requires an authenticated/seeded deployment and the actual detail-page slugs. It has been added but has not yet been run against all requested routes/viewports. Screenshots and a zero-intersection claim will only be reported after the browser audit executes successfully.

title: PERF-1: route skeletons, image optimization and Lighthouse reporting
head: perf/perf-1-loading-images-lighthouse
body: ## PERF-1 progress This PR adds targeted improvements and a reproducible before/after measurement pipeline. It does **not** claim all performance targets are already met. ### Included - Adds page-shaped loading fallbacks for Search, Teams, Team Detail and Dashboard. The global fallback remains unchanged so it does not show a misleading Home skeleton on unrelated routes. - Enables Next.js AVIF/WebP optimization for the Home hero image by removing `unoptimized` and allowing the exact Unsplash host. - Makes Follow, Review Like and HoopFeed Check actions optimistic, with rollback on request failure. - Adds an independent CI performance comparison job that builds both the PR base revision and candidate revision, records the Next build route-size table, and runs three mobile Lighthouse passes each for Home, Search and a representative Team Detail route. It reports the 90 Performance / 2.5s LCP / 0.1 CLS targets as warnings and uploads both result sets. ### Still outstanding before PERF-1 can be called complete - Home is a static client-rendered page; it does not fetch page data. The global route fallback remains the existing loader. Route-specific loading shapes are added for the data-heavy directory and account screens listed above, not every route in the app. - App Router already provides route-level splitting. The before/after build output must be reviewed to identify shared-chunk weight and any genuinely removable one-feature dependency. - Team/avatar/poster URLs have multiple origins and several are raw `` elements. Full modernization requires an origin inventory, correct per-box sizing, and browser verification; this PR only optimizes the known Home hero asset. - Search queries are limited and the team directory already uses range-based pagination. Team Detail currently receives and renders the full approved review array, and Live Games can load up to 500 games. Safe review pagination/virtualization still needs a paginated review UI and a defined live-game window without hiding data. - Repeat-visit data caching, prefetch policy, font network transfer/weight traces, and scroll-jank profiling still need verification. Next.js Link prefetch is already used for normal internal links. - Before/after metrics will be added after the independent CI comparison finishes. No score is claimed yet. The existing main CI currently has unrelated baseline failures (hardcoded-surface audit and an ESLint error in `app/admin/team-fanfeed/page.tsx`); the performance job is independent and does not bypass or weaken those gates. No production merge or deployment is included.

title: Document safe Apple IAP implementation contract
head: feat/apple-iap-foundation
body:
## Summary
Builds a staged, isolated foundation for HoopCheck's Apple auto-renewable subscriptions while preserving the live Stripe billing path.

- Adds an additive, unapplied Supabase migration for server-only Apple account-token, transaction, subscription, and notification-ledger tables.
- Adds server-issued `appAccountToken` mapping and fail-closed ownership / entitlement-candidate helpers.
- Adds product/environment allowlisting and notification orchestration with duplicate handling and retry behavior.
- Adds an adapter for Apple's `SignedDataVerifier` interface, plus mock-based adapter contract tests.
- Prevents caching of authenticated Apple account-token API responses with `Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0`.
- Adds a static security-contract test for the account-token endpoint and runs it in CI.
- Adds `docs/apple-iap-release-runbook.md` with Apple account setup, server config, notification, mobile integration, verification gates, and rollback checklist.
- Keeps Pro $4.99/month and Premium $9.99/month; does not overwrite Stripe-owned subscription columns.

## Validation
- Latest previously reported CI on commit `285e74fc3e54fe2cd3953286d546641cb8711bfb`: Apple IAP regression tests, launch-test, mobile typecheck, and main build all passed.
- The new runbook documentation commit is `4876a86678df39b50f11466d9880a9a5a18de1e0`; checks for this new commit must complete before treating the branch as green.

These are repository checks only. Static route assertions and mock tests do not prove live Supabase integration, real Apple signature verification, transaction reconciliation, StoreKit purchase/restore, or an iOS native cloud build.

## Remaining release blockers
- Apple app record and subscription products have not been created; permanent bundle ID and exact product IDs are still required.
- The official `@apple/app-store-server-library` package is not yet installed and wired into a production route.
- Server notification persistence/reconciliation must bind verified transactions to HoopCheck users and update Apple-owned entitlement records idempotently.
- Native StoreKit purchase and restore flows, a cloud iOS development build, and sandbox-device testing remain incomplete.
- The additive migration has not been applied to any database; full entitlement/RLS audit remains required before release.

## Release safety
- Draft PR only; not merged or deployed.
- No production database migration or production billing settings were changed.
- No Stripe entitlements or prices were changed; existing Stripe memberships must continue to be honored.
- Apple purchase UI remains disabled until the remaining release blockers are completed and verified.

This is still a bootstrap and has not been built or tested on Xcode/iPhone. The PR does not generate the iOS project, configure Apple Associated Domains/AASA, implement push token registration or backend APNs delivery. The existing Next.js app uses server functionality, so static export must not be enabled without an architecture audit. A remote-only wrapper may still fail App Review Guideline 4.2; native value must be tested and demonstrated before submission.

## Required next steps
1. Confirm the branch's GitHub Actions checks pass; Vercel deployment checks are not release proof.
2. On a Mac with Xcode, generate and configure the iOS target and signing (not possible from an iPhone-only workflow).
3. Configure universal links and test cold/warm launch routing on a physical device.
4. Verify native share on each profile route and validate player/agent route patterns.
5. Implement opt-in push registration and secure backend delivery.
6. Validate auth, account deletion, privacy disclosures, and compliant membership billing.
7. Test through TestFlight; do not merge/deploy or submit publicly until checks pass and owner approves.
